history: Write a fictional adult outpatient history with three consultations. Separate intended events from what is reported at each consultation. State what is omitted, uncertain or documented late. Keep source material out of this seed-free exercise.
documentation: Use the assigned writing style. Plan the content of each consultation without changing the intended clinical events to suit the style. Include ordinary follow-up. Leave missing outcomes missing and distinguish a patient report from a clinician's interpretation.
letters: Write the three letters from the consultation plans. Preserve the assigned visit and availability dates. State medication plans, actual use and investigation results separately. Keep repeated or disputed accounts identifiable. Retain each draft when revising it.
annotation: Read only the finished letters supplied for this task. Extract statements using the supplied annotation guide and schema. Quote the exact text supporting each statement, its time and any relationship. Preserve uncertain dates, separate reporters and different event patterns. Hidden authoring history cannot fill a gap in the letters.
queries: For each supplied question and date, read only the letters available by its information cutoff. Return eligible when the text supports the predicate, ineligible when it supports that the predicate is false, and indeterminate when information is missing or conflicting. Give exact evidence and a reason. Later text may explain an earlier decision but cannot change when it happened.
